name: Keychain item stored with kSecAttrAccessibleAlways
task_triggers: storing credentials or tokens in the Keychain
attack_scenario: An attacker who obtains a locked device or an unencrypted backup extracts the keychain item without the passcode, because 'Always' items are decrypted with a key not tied to device unlock — yielding the stored token or password.
negative_test_hint: store a token with the "kSecAttrAccessibleAlways" protection class and assert reading it back from a locked device or an unencrypted backup fails

exemplar.explanation: kSecAttrAccessibleAlways (and its AlwaysThisDeviceOnly variant) makes the keychain item decryptable even while the device is locked, so it is not protected by the passcode-derived key and is included in unencrypted backups. kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly ties decryption to device unlock and keeps the item off backups and off other devices, which is what Apple, OWASP MSTG-STORAGE-2, and CWE-522 require.
